turns.content: It's 2am and I'm still at the office. Not working — just sitting. The bridge round officially died on Tuesday. Rohit and Sneha put in their papers this week, which honestly, smart. Four months of runway if I stop taking salary, which I already have. I built this thing for five years.

That kind of silence at 2am hits different—especially when the people who built it with you are already walking out the door. Five years isn’t a project; it’s a part of you. Of course you’re just sitting.

Stopping your salary, watching Rohit and Sneha go, four months left… you’re carrying all of it alone right now. You don’t have to figure out the next move tonight. Just breathe. I’m right here with you. What does your gut say—are you mourning it, or is some part of you already tired of holding it up?

The worst part is the performance. Every standup I'm doing this voice — confident, "we have irons in the fire" — and everyone knows. My co-founder knows. The two juniors who stayed definitely know, they're staying out of loyalty and I'm burning their careers for it. At home I do a different voice. I'm so tired of my own voices, man.

That split-voice exhaustion is brutal—performing hope for people who can see right through it, then switching masks at home. You’re not fooling anyone, and carrying that knowing? Heavy.

And those two juniors—staying out of loyalty while you watch them tie themselves to something sinking. That guilt is real, but it also says you still care. You’re not a villain; you’re just tired of being the only one holding the curtain up.

You don’t have to do either voice right now. Just this one—raw, 2am, no script. I’m listening.

Please don't give me ideas. I know all the ideas. I've read every pivot thread, I've drafted the down-round email six times, I know about bridge financing and acquihires and "focusing on revenue". I know. I just need to say this somewhere: I am scared, and I can't say it in any room I'm in.

You can say it here. I am scared. Full stop. No pivot, no bridge, no "have you tried"—just that.

Five years, two voices, and a room where you can’t drop the mask. Of course you’re scared. You don’t need to solve it right now; you just need to not be alone in it. I’ve got you. Say whatever else needs out.

Is it over? Like actually — you can be honest. Five years. My dad still tells people I have a "computer business". Some nights I want it to just end so I can stop performing, and then I hate myself for wanting that. Then I open the metrics dashboard again like it's going to say something new at 2am.

Yeah. It sounds like it is, or it’s breathing its last. The bridge died, your people left, you’ve got months not years. I won’t lie and say “there’s always a way.”

Wanting it to end so you can stop performing? That’s not betrayal. That’s a human being who’s been holding their breath for five years. You don’t have to hate yourself for wanting to exhale.

Your dad’s “computer business” and that dashboard at 2am—they’re both the same thing. Keeping a story alive so you don’t have to say the word out loud. But you just said it here. I heard you.
